chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ibn Mahbub, from Jamil ibn Salih, from Abu Ubaydah, who said:
“Bring me a Book before this, or traces of knowledge, if you are truthful.”
He said: “By the Book, He meant the Tawrah and the Injil; and by ‘traces of knowledge’, He only meant by that the knowledge of the successors of the Prophets (عليهم السلام).”

key_terms.أَثَارَةٍ: A trace or remnant; here meaning a remaining transmitted legacy of knowledge.
key_terms.أَوْصِيَاءِ: Successors or legatees entrusted with preserving divine knowledge.
key_terms.التَّوْرَاةَ: The Torah, one of the earlier revealed scriptures.
key_terms.الْأَنْبِيَاءِ: The Prophets, upon whom be peace.
key_terms.الْإِنْجِيلَ: The Gospel, one of the earlier revealed scriptures.
key_terms.عِلْمٍ: Knowledge; here sacred knowledge inherited through divinely appointed successors.
key_terms.كِتَابٍ: A revealed scripture; here referring to earlier divine books.

ai.seo_question: What does “أَوْ أَثَارَةٍ مِنْ عِلْمٍ” mean in Qur'an 46:4 according to Imam al-Baqir (عليه السلام)?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the Qur'anic phrase about bringing a prior book or a trace of knowledge. Imam Abu Ja‘far (عليه السلام) states that the “Book” refers to the Tawrah and the Injil, while “traces of knowledge” refers to the transmitted knowledge of the awsiya' of the Prophets (عليهم السلام).

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel Bin Salih, from Abu Ubeyda who said,
about the Words of the Exalted
[46:4] Bring me a Book before this or traces of the Knowledge, if you are truthful.
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It Means by the Book, the Torah, and the Evangel, ‘traces of knowledge’, so rather it means by that, knowledge of the successors<sup>as</sup> of the Prophets<sup>as</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 72. Al-Husayn ibn muhammad has narrated from from Mu‘alla ibn Muhammad from the one who had narrated to him from Ali ibnja who has said the following.

“I heard abu al-Hassan (a.s.) say, ‘When the Messenger of Allah saw Taym, ‘Adi and Amawids climb his pulpit he was severely frightened. Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, sent him a reading to comfort him.

“When We told the angels to prostrate before Adam they all obeyed except Iblis (Satan) who refused.” [20:116] Then Allah, sent him a message that said, “O Muhammad, commanded them and they disobeyed. Do not despair if you will command them and they will disobey you in the matters of the executor of your will.”
